description: Round and sand-pale, balancing one bright drop on a stalk. The drop is the weapon and comes round like a flail.
lore: The collectors call all the round ones lings, one word for the same business turning up in five kinds of country, and the low country's is pale as dry sand, holding a single bright drop up over itself on a stalk. Of everything a wet field at first light contains, the drop on its stem with the sun inside is the detail everyone keeps exactly; the rest wears down under all that remembering to pale grain, no particular grass, no particular year.

It swings the drop round like a weight on a line, catching the light as it comes, meaning none of it. The trade's one rule is to work with the sun at your back, because whoever is looking into the flash when the blow lands loses the next few steps of the fight. Flattened, it leaves no body at all, just [[items/pale_sand_stone|something sun-bleached and far too heavy]] lying in the pressed grass.

Most mornings one comes partway up the rise toward the fire on [[lore/the_waking|the meadow where everyone wakes]] and stops just short of the light, and the fire's oldest joke is that it has come to be met. [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] lets the joke stand. But after a night when the fire sat ready and the meadow stayed empty, she has been seen walking down the wet field to stand beside it a while, and whatever she says there she has never once brought back up the hill.
